name: Intercontinental Exchange
desc: Operates financial exchanges and clearing houses, including the New York Stock Exchange, plus market data and mortgage technology.
markets: Exchanges, clearing and data services across the US, Europe and Asia; global institutional and mortgage-industry customers.
rationale: Global financial-markets brand could use F1 B2B hospitality and visibility, as Nasdaq does with its F1 partnership.
changed: Acquired Black Knight in 2023

name: CMOC Group
desc: Mines and produces copper, cobalt, molybdenum, tungsten, niobium and phosphates, with major mines in Congo and Brazil.
markets: Mines in China, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Brazil; sells metals to industrial buyers worldwide, including through trader IXM.
rationale: B2B commodity miner without consumer brand; F1 offers little beyond corporate hospitality; weak fit.
changed: Renamed CMOC Group from China Molybdenum in 2022

name: Gerdau
desc: Produces long steel products such as rebar, wire rod, structural shapes and special steels, mostly from recycled scrap.
markets: Sales split mainly between Brazil and North America, with further operations elsewhere in South America.
rationale: B2B steelmaker with limited marketing; possible Brazil and US hospitality use, but weak overall F1 fit.

name: Rio Tinto
desc: Mines and processes iron ore, aluminium, copper, lithium and other minerals for steelmakers and industrial customers worldwide.
markets: Operations in Australia, Canada, the Americas, Africa and Europe; sells mainly to Asian, especially Chinese, industrial buyers.
rationale: Commodity miner with little consumer marketing; F1 could serve corporate hospitality in Asia and Australia only; weak fit.
changed: Acquired Arcadium Lithium in 2025

name: Anglo American
desc: Mines copper, iron ore and other minerals, selling to smelters, steelmakers and industrial buyers worldwide.
markets: Mines in South America, southern Africa and Australia; customers across Asia, Europe and elsewhere.
rationale: B2B miner with little consumer marketing; De Beers is being sold; weak F1 fit beyond hospitality.
changed: Demerged Valterra Platinum in 2025; agreed merger with Teck Resources in 2025 to form Anglo Teck

name: Tata Steel
desc: Produces flat and long steel for automotive, construction and engineering customers, with plants in India and Europe.
markets: Steelmaking in India, the Netherlands and the UK, plus South-East Asian operations; exports widely.
rationale: Tata group brand with sports sponsorship culture; F1 could support B2B relations in Europe and India.

name: Teck Resources
desc: Mines copper and zinc in Canada, the US, Chile and Peru for smelters and industrial buyers.
markets: Mines in Canada, Alaska, Chile and Peru; sells concentrates and metals mainly to Asian smelters.
rationale: B2B miner with no consumer brand and a pending merger; weak F1 fit.
changed: Sold steelmaking coal business to Glencore in 2024; agreed merger with Anglo American in 2025

name: JSW Steel
desc: Produces flat and long steel for construction, automotive, appliance and infrastructure customers from integrated plants in India.
markets: Mainly India, with steel operations in the United States and Italy and exports to other markets.
rationale: JSW Group invests in sport; F1 could build profile with Indian and international B2B customers.

name: POSCO
desc: Produces flat steel, stainless steel and specialty steel for carmakers, shipbuilders, appliance makers and construction customers.
markets: Steelworks in Korea plus plants and processing centres in Asia, the Americas and Europe; global automotive customers.
rationale: Major supplier to global carmakers; F1 could support automotive steel showcase and Korean B2B hospitality.
changed: Split in 2022 into listed holding company POSCO Holdings and wholly owned steel unit POSCO

name: AngloGold Ashanti
desc: Mines gold at operations in Africa, Australia and the Americas, selling output mainly to bullion refiners.
markets: Mines in Ghana, Guinea, Tanzania, Egypt, Congo, Australia, Brazil and Argentina; gold sold to refiners.
rationale: Gold producer without consumer products; weak F1 fit beyond limited corporate hospitality.
changed: Moved primary listing to NYSE and corporate base to US in 2023; acquired Centamin (Sukari mine) in 2024

name: Dauch
desc: Supplies driveline, axle, metal-forming and powder metal components to car and truck manufacturers worldwide.
markets: Plants and customers across North America, Europe, Asia and South America, serving global vehicle makers.
rationale: Driveline supplier to carmakers; F1 could offer engineering showcase and OEM hospitality, though brand is new.
changed: American Axle & Manufacturing acquired Dowlais Group (GKN Automotive) in 2025 and renamed itself Dauch

name: CEMEX
desc: Produces and sells cement, ready-mix concrete and aggregates to builders and construction firms in many countries.
markets: Operates in Mexico, the US, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Latin America.
rationale: Strong Mexican and US brand among builders; F1 races in Mexico City and US offer hospitality use.

name: SpaceX
desc: Builds and launches rockets and spacecraft, runs the Starlink satellite internet service, and provides AI services through xAI.
markets: Launch customers worldwide; Starlink subscribers in over 100 countries across all major regions.
rationale: Highly visible technology brand; Starlink consumer growth could use F1 technology showcase, though it seldom buys sponsorship.
changed: Combined with xAI in 2026; listing status not confirmed

name: Evonik Industries
desc: Produces specialty chemicals, additives, silica and amino acids for consumer goods, automotive, health and animal-feed makers.
markets: Production and sales across Europe, the Americas and Asia, in over 100 countries.
rationale: Experienced football sponsor (Borussia Dortmund); F1 could serve automotive and B2B hospitality, but fit is moderate.

name: PPG Industries
desc: Makes paints, coatings and specialty materials for automotive, aerospace, industrial and architectural customers worldwide.
markets: Operates in more than 70 countries across North America, Europe, Asia and Latin America.
rationale: Automotive coatings supplier; rival Sherwin-Williams and AkzoNobel brands sponsor F1, making a strong fit.
changed: Sold US and Canada architectural paints business, including Glidden and Olympic, in 2024

name: Celanese
desc: Produces acetyl chemicals and engineered polymers for automotive, medical, electronics, paints and consumer goods manufacturers.
markets: Production and customers across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Engineered polymers for carmakers give a technology tie-in, but low marketing culture; plausible fit.
changed: Acquired DuPont Mobility & Materials business in 2022

name: BHP
desc: Mines and sells iron ore, copper, metallurgical coal and potash to steelmakers and manufacturers worldwide.
markets: Mines in Australia, Chile, Peru and Canada; sells largely to Chinese and other Asian buyers.
rationale: Commodity miner with no consumer brand; F1 offers limited value beyond Australian hospitality; weak fit.

name: Sasol
desc: Produces fuels, chemicals and gas from coal and natural gas, and runs fuel stations in South Africa.
markets: Fuels mainly in South Africa; gas in Mozambique; chemical plants in the US and Europe.
rationale: Former F1 sponsor (BMW Sauber); South African fuel brand with limited markets where F1 races; plausible fit.

name: Sasol
desc: Produces fuels, chemicals and gas from coal and natural gas, and runs fuel stations in South Africa.
markets: Fuels mainly in South Africa; gas in Mozambique; chemical plants in the US and Europe.
rationale: Former F1 sponsor (BMW Sauber); South African fuel brand with limited markets where F1 races; plausible fit.

name: Amcor
desc: Makes flexible and rigid plastic packaging, bottles and closures for food, beverage, healthcare and consumer goods companies.
markets: Plants and customers across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: B2B packaging supplier to consumer brands; limited marketing culture; plausible but weak F1 fit.
changed: Completed merger with Berry Global in 2025

name: Covestro
desc: Produces polycarbonate and polyurethane raw materials for automotive, construction, electronics and furniture manufacturers.
markets: Production and sales across Europe, Asia and the Americas.
rationale: Materials supplier to carmakers under Gulf ownership; possible F1 technology tie-in, moderate fit.
changed: Acquired by ADNOC through XRG in 2025

name: Air Liquide
desc: Supplies industrial and medical gases, related equipment and home healthcare services to industry and hospitals.
markets: Operates in more than 70 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: Hydrogen and technology story plus global B2B customer base; F1 hospitality and sustainability tie-in plausible.

name: Chemours
desc: Makes titanium dioxide pigment, refrigerants and fluoropolymers such as Teflon for paint, cooling and electronics manufacturers.
markets: 28 production sites in 8 countries, serving about 2,400 customers in roughly 110 countries.
rationale: B2B chemicals maker facing PFAS litigation, with limited marketing spend and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Clariant
desc: Produces specialty chemicals including catalysts, adsorbents, additives and care chemicals for industrial and consumer goods makers.
markets: Subsidiaries in 36 countries, with sites in Europe, North America, South America, China and India.
rationale: B2B specialty chemicals supplier with low marketing spend and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit beyond hospitality.

name: Hithium Energy Storage
desc: Makes lithium iron phosphate battery cells and containerised energy storage systems for utilities and renewable energy developers.
markets: Sells storage systems in China and abroad, including the US, Europe, the Middle East and Australia.
rationale: Fast-growing Chinese storage brand seeking international utility customers; an F1 sustainability and technology showcase is plausible.
changed: Filed for a Hong Kong listing in 2025; outcome not confirmed

name: Air Products and Chemicals
desc: Supplies industrial gases such as hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen, plus related equipment, to refining, chemicals and electronics customers.
markets: Operations in about 50 countries across the Americas, Europe, Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: B2B gas supplier with hydrogen projects; limited marketing culture; plausible but not obvious F1 fit.

name: Arkema
desc: Produces specialty materials, adhesives (Bostik), high-performance polymers and coatings for construction, batteries, transport and electronics.
markets: Sites in about 55 countries across Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Bostik and performance polymers offer technology tie-in, but mainly B2B; plausible fit.

name: Syensqo
desc: Produces specialty polymers, composites and battery materials for aerospace, automotive, electronics and consumer goods makers.
markets: Production and customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia.
rationale: Composites and lightweight materials offer a direct F1 technology tie-in for automotive and aerospace customers.
changed: Spun off from Solvay in 2023

name: Orbia
desc: Makes PVC and polymer products, Wavin pipes, Netafim drip irrigation, fluorochemicals and data communication products.
markets: Operations and customers in about 50 countries across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Asia.
rationale: Industrial group with Wavin and Netafim brands; F1 Mexico City race offers hospitality, but fit is moderate.
changed: Renamed Orbia from Mexichem in 2019

name: Eastman Chemical
desc: Produces specialty plastics, additives, fibres and chemicals, including Tritan copolyester, for packaging, building, automotive and consumer goods.
markets: Operates 36 manufacturing sites worldwide, serving customers in the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Specialty materials with automotive uses and recycling story; mostly B2B; plausible but modest fit.

name: Maire
desc: Designs and builds plants for fertilisers, polymers, gas processing and hydrogen, and licenses process technologies through NextChem.
markets: Projects for energy and industrial clients in the Middle East, Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas.
rationale: B2B engineering contractor; F1 hospitality could reach Gulf energy clients, but fit is moderate.
changed: Renamed Maire from Maire Tecnimont in 2023

name: Worley
desc: Provides engineering, design, project delivery and consulting services to energy, chemicals and resources companies worldwide.
markets: Operations in around 40 countries across Australia, the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Asia.
rationale: B2B engineering firm; F1 could support client hospitality with energy majors, but fit is weak.
changed: Acquired Jacobs Energy, Chemicals and Resources business in 2019

name: Henkel
desc: Makes adhesives such as Loctite plus consumer brands like Persil, Schwarzkopf, Dial and Pritt.
markets: Operates in more than 70 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia and Africa.
rationale: Big consumer and industrial brand owner and active sponsor; Loctite adhesives give automotive tie-in; strong fit.

name: PTT Global Chemical
desc: Produces olefins, polyethylene, polypropylene, aromatics and bioplastics for packaging, automotive and industrial manufacturers.
markets: Mainly Thailand, with operations in the US, Europe and China, including coatings resins maker allnex.
rationale: B2B petrochemicals subsidiary of state energy group; Thai market interest but weak F1 fit.
changed: Acquired allnex in 2021

name: Johnson Matthey
desc: Makes vehicle emission control catalysts, hydrogen technologies and platinum group metal products and services for industrial customers.
markets: Operations and customers across Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Automotive catalyst and hydrogen technology offer a tie-in; B2B with limited marketing; plausible fit.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to sell Catalyst Technologies to Honeywell

name: Entegris
desc: Supplies filters, high-purity chemicals, materials and wafer containers to semiconductor manufacturers and equipment makers.
markets: Facilities in the US, Asia and Europe, serving chipmakers in Taiwan, Korea, the US and elsewhere.
rationale: Niche B2B chip-materials supplier with no consumer brand and little marketing; weak F1 fit beyond hospitality.
changed: Acquired CMC Materials in 2022

name: Indorama Ventures
desc: Produces PET resin, polyester fibres and intermediate petrochemicals for beverage, packaging, textile and tyre-cord manufacturers.
markets: Plants across Asia, Europe, the Americas and Africa, supplying global beverage and textile companies.
rationale: B2B petrochemicals supplier; recycling story could link to sustainability, but F1 fit is weak.

name: CNH Industrial
desc: Makes agricultural and construction equipment under brands including Case IH, New Holland, Steyr and CASE.
markets: Factories in North America, Europe and Brazil; sells through dealers worldwide, including Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Strong equipment brands among farmers and builders; F1 dealer hospitality plausible, though rivals rarely sponsor.
changed: Spun off Iveco in 2022; delisted from Euronext Milan in 2024

name: Morton Salt
desc: Produces salt for food, water softening, road de-icing, agriculture and industrial use in North America.
markets: Customers in the United States and Canada; no verified expansion plans beyond North America.
rationale: Well-known US household brand, but low-margin commodity; F1 US races give limited value; weak fit.
changed: Acquired from K+S by Stone Canyon Industries in 2021

name: Nordex
desc: Designs, makes and sells onshore wind turbines and provides service for wind farm developers and operators.
markets: Turbines installed in over 40 countries; production in Germany, Spain, Brazil, India and Mexico.
rationale: B2B turbine maker with sustainability story but little marketing culture; weak to plausible fit.
changed: Merged with Acciona Windpower in 2016

name: ADNOC
desc: Produces oil and gas and operates refining, petrochemicals, fuel retail, shipping and trading through subsidiaries.
markets: Exports energy to Asian, European and other markets; fuel retail in the UAE; growing international chemical assets.
rationale: Gulf energy giant with home Grand Prix in Abu Dhabi; rival Aramco sponsors F1; strong fit.
changed: Acquired Covestro through XRG in 2025

name: Ball Corporation
desc: Makes aluminium beverage cans and bottles for soft drink, beer and other beverage companies worldwide.
markets: Plants in North America, South America, Europe and other regions; supplies major global drinks brands.
rationale: B2B can maker with sustainability message; limited consumer marketing; plausible but weak F1 fit.
changed: Sold aerospace business to BAE Systems in 2024

name: Crown Holdings
desc: Makes aluminium beverage cans, food cans, aerosol cans and transit packaging for consumer goods companies.
markets: Plants across the Americas, Europe and Asia, supplying food and drinks makers worldwide.
rationale: B2B packaging supplier with little consumer marketing; F1 offers only limited client hospitality value; weak fit.
changed: Moved headquarters from Pennsylvania to Tampa, Florida in 2023

name: Bureau Veritas
desc: Provides testing, inspection and certification for buildings, industrial plants, ships, commodities and consumer products.
markets: Operates in about 140 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia, Africa and the Middle East.
rationale: B2B services firm with modest marketing; F1 could support corporate hospitality; plausible but weak fit.

name: Kawasaki Heavy Industries
desc: Makes motorcycles, aircraft components, rolling stock, ships, gas turbines, industrial robots and hydrogen equipment.
markets: Sells motorcycles worldwide and supplies industrial and defence customers in Japan, Asia, the Americas and Europe.
rationale: Motorsport-minded Kawasaki brand with robotics and hydrogen technology; strong for Japanese and global audiences.

name: International Flavors & Fragrances
desc: Creates flavours, fragrances, food ingredients, enzymes and probiotics for food, beverage, household and personal care makers.
markets: Creative, sales and production sites worldwide across the Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa.
rationale: B2B ingredients supplier with no consumer-facing brand of its own; F1 offers limited value; weak fit.
changed: Merged with DuPont Nutrition & Biosciences in 2021

name: Avery Dennison
desc: Makes pressure-sensitive labels, apparel branding tags, RFID inlays and graphics materials for retail, logistics and consumer brands.
markets: Operations in over 50 countries across the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: RFID and digital identification tie-in for apparel and merchandise; mainly B2B; plausible fit.

name: Polaris
desc: Makes off-road vehicles, snowmobiles, Slingshot three-wheelers and pontoon boats sold through dealers to consumers and businesses.
markets: Mainly North America, with dealers and sales in Europe, Asia-Pacific and other markets.
rationale: Consumer powersports brand with racing heritage; US races fit, but core market differs from F1; plausible.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to sell majority of Indian Motorcycle to Carolwood

name: Veralto
desc: Provides water analytics and treatment equipment plus product marking, coding, packaging and colour technologies.
markets: Customers in utilities, industry and consumer goods across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B instrument and water technology maker with modest marketing spend; F1 offers limited value; weak fit.
changed: Spun off from Danaher in 2023

name: Unitree Robotics
desc: Makes quadruped robot dogs and humanoid robots for research, education, entertainment and industrial customers.
markets: Sells robots in China and internationally, including to researchers and developers in North America and Europe.
rationale: Viral robotics brand seeking global profile; F1 technology showcase plausible, though still a young company.
changed: Began preparing a Shanghai STAR Market listing in 2025; outcome not confirmed

name: Axalta Coating Systems
desc: Makes liquid and powder coatings for car refinish, new vehicles, commercial vehicles and industrial uses.
markets: Plants and customers across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: Automotive refinish brands with motorsport heritage; rivals Glasurit and Sikkens sponsor F1; strong fit.
changed: Carved out of DuPont in 2013; agreed merger with AkzoNobel in 2025

name: Pandora
desc: Designs, makes and sells charm bracelets, rings and lab-grown diamond jewellery through its own stores and retailers.
markets: Sold in about 100 countries; key markets are the US, Europe, Australia and growing Asian markets.
rationale: Global consumer brand with heavy marketing; F1's growing female audience could fit, plausible partnership.

name: Hitachi
desc: Provides digital systems and IT services, power grid equipment, railway systems and industrial products to businesses and governments.
markets: Operations and customers across Japan, Asia, North America and Europe, including Hitachi Rail and Hitachi Energy.
rationale: Global B2B technology brand with data and energy story; F1 technology partnerships plausible and fit Japan.

name: JK Tyre & Industries
desc: Makes truck, bus, passenger car, two-wheeler and farm tyres sold through dealers in India and abroad.
markets: Mainly India, with plants in Mexico and exports to other markets.
rationale: Tyre brand with Indian motorsport involvement; F1 appeals to Indian fans, but budget may be limited.

name: Metso
desc: Supplies crushers, grinding mills, flotation and filtration equipment, spare parts and services to mining and aggregates customers.
markets: Operates in about 50 countries across Europe, the Americas, Africa, Asia and Australia.
rationale: B2B equipment maker for mining customers with low marketing culture; F1 offers limited value; weak fit.
changed: Formed by merger of Metso Minerals and Outotec in 2020; renamed Metso in 2023

name: Bahri
desc: Transports crude oil, chemicals, dry bulk and general cargo by sea and offers logistics services.
markets: Ships crude and chemicals from Saudi Arabia to Asia, Europe and the Americas.
rationale: Saudi national carrier; Saudi Arabian Grand Prix and Aramco links make F1 hospitality plausible.
changed: Renamed Bahri from National Shipping Company of Saudi Arabia

name: HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering
desc: Intermediate holding company of HD Hyundai's shipyards, which build LNG carriers, container ships, tankers and naval vessels.
markets: Shipyards in Korea serving shipowners and navies in Europe, Asia, the Middle East and the Americas.
rationale: B2B shipbuilder; F1 hospitality could reach global shipowners, but fit is weak.

name: Ciena
desc: Makes optical and packet networking equipment and software for telecom carriers, cloud providers, governments and enterprises.
markets: Customers across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: Networking technology tie-in with F1 data transmission; rivals in networking sponsor F1; plausible to strong fit.

name: FedEx
desc: Provides express parcel, ground and freight delivery, e-commerce logistics and business services in over 220 countries.
markets: Worldwide network across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and the Middle East.
rationale: Global logistics brand; rival DHL is F1 logistics partner; strong B2B and consumer fit.
changed: Announced spin-off of FedEx Freight in 2024

name: Gopuff
desc: Delivers convenience-store goods, snacks, drinks, alcohol and household items to consumers via its app.
markets: Operates in more than 500 US cities; any current operations outside the US not confirmed.
rationale: US consumer app brand; US Grands Prix could suit, but domestic focus limits value; plausible.

name: Prologis
desc: Owns, develops and leases logistics warehouses to retailers, e-commerce, logistics and manufacturing companies.
markets: Properties in about 20 countries across the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B landlord with little consumer marketing; F1 hospitality for logistics tenants plausible but weak.

name: J&T Express
desc: Provides express parcel delivery and cross-border logistics for e-commerce sellers and consumers.
markets: South-East Asia, China, Latin America and the Middle East.
rationale: Fast-growing consumer-facing logistics brand in emerging markets; F1 races in Asia and Latin America fit.
changed: Listed in Hong Kong in 2023

name: HelloFresh
desc: Delivers meal kits and ready-to-eat meals to subscribers under HelloFresh, Factor, Green Chef and EveryPlate.
markets: Operates in the US, Canada, Western Europe, Australia and New Zealand.
rationale: Heavy consumer advertiser across F1's core markets; F1 could drive subscriptions; strong fit.

name: Heidelberg Materials
desc: Produces cement, aggregates and ready-mixed concrete for construction and infrastructure firms, and develops carbon capture.
markets: Operations in about 50 countries across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and Africa.
rationale: B2B building materials group with low marketing culture; F1 offers only limited client hospitality value; weak fit.
changed: Renamed from HeidelbergCement in 2022

name: Saint-Gobain
desc: Makes glass, insulation, plasterboard, mortars and construction chemicals, and distributes building materials to builders and industry.
markets: Operates in about 75 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia and Africa.
rationale: Large B2B building brand with some consumer awareness; F1 hospitality plausible but not obvious.

name: Ferretti Group
desc: Designs, builds and sells luxury motor yachts under Ferretti Yachts, Riva, Pershing, Wally, CRN and other brands.
markets: Sells yachts to wealthy buyers in Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Luxury brand reaching the same wealthy audience as F1 Paddock Club; Monaco and Miami fit; strong.
changed: Listed in Hong Kong in 2022 and Milan in 2023

name: BlueScope
desc: Makes coated and painted steel such as COLORBOND and ZINCALUME, plus building products and steel for construction.
markets: Operations in Australia, New Zealand, North America and Asia.
rationale: COLORBOND is a familiar Australian brand; Australian Grand Prix hospitality plausible, but fit is limited.
changed: Spun off from BHP Billiton in 2002

name: Jacobs
desc: Provides engineering, consulting and project management for infrastructure, water, advanced facilities and environmental clients.
markets: Operations across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B consulting firm; F1 could support client hospitality and technology messaging, but fit is moderate.
changed: Spun off government services into Amentum in 2024
